source.method: Disassembly listings from capstone 5.0.7 over the pinned image and ghidra-cli 0.2.2 queries on Ghidra 12.1.4 were treated as leads. Every instruction sequence, table and string below is confirmed against the pinned bytes by tools/verify_scb_clip_classes.py --exe. The install census and invariants are recomputed by tools/verify_scb_clip_classes.py --install.

registry.boundary: The registry object is u32(u32(S+0x6c))+8 for the singleton S returned by 0x00a02360, the same object the published layout page names. outcomes.claim: The base registrar 0x00a4c2a0 inserts SetPosClip (factory 0x00a4db10), ShowHideClip (0x00a4db80), MotionClip (0x00a4dcd0), ClipSyncClip (0x0063c570) and LocalCameraClip (0x00a4d950) through 0x0063f710. Manager slot 3 at 0x00635760 calls it at 0x00635899 and then inserts the Rapture group. In that group RapturePhysicsLookAtClip (0x0063a5f0) is a new key. SetPosClip (0x0063bd90), ShowHideClip (0x0063bf40) and MotionClip (0x0063c180) are each preceded by a call to 0x0063f920 with a second copy of the key literal. Both groups address the registry object reached through the singleton returned by 0x00a02360.

Insertion keeps the earlier factory for an equal key, and the call to 0x0063f920 before each of the three Rapture re-registrations is read as erase by key. The registry then holds the Rapture factories for SetPosClip, ShowHideClip and MotionClip, and the base factories for ClipSyncClip and LocalCameraClip. The body of 0x0063f920 was not walked.

Each factory stores its object size when the size argument is nonnull. The sizes are 0x38 for SetPosClip, ShowHideClip, RapturePhysicsLookAtClip, RaptureNqMotionBlendOnOffClip, RaptureFacialPoseForSchClip, RaptureFacialLipSyncClip and KillClip, 0x58 for RaptureMesClip, 0x60 for MotionClip and DepthOfFieldClip, 0x3c for ClipSyncClip and 0x120 for LocalCameraClip. Each constructor installs the primary vtable at +0 and a secondary table at +8. In every primary vtable slot 1 calls the base method 0x00a20f30, which stores state 1 at clip +0x1c. Slot 2 is the update method. Slot 29 returns a class-specific address relative to D. It is the record end for SetPosClip, ShowHideClip, MotionClip, RaptureNqMotionBlendOnOffClip, RaptureFacialPoseForSchClip and RaptureFacialLipSyncClip. It is not the record end for the other classes, as listed per class.

Base accessors read s16(D+8) in slot 22, u8(D+0x0a) in slot 23, bits 0, 1 and 2 of u8(D+0x0b) in slots 25, 27 and 26, and s16(D+0x0c) in slot 20, beside the u8(D+2), u8(D+3) and u32(D+4) readers in slots 5, 6 and 7. Slot 7 is the clip start tick. Slot 8 is the clip end tick and jumps through slot 7 unless a class overrides it. MotionClip returns u32(D+0x18), DepthOfFieldClip returns u32(D+0x10) and LocalCameraClip returns u32(D+0x10) plus clip +0x110. Base slots 3 and 4 store state 3 and state 4, and the update method moves state 1 to state 2.

RaptureSetPosClip slot 1 at 0x0082a080 resolves the actor record, casts its slot 23 result from IActor to CharaActor, and fetches three vectors from the object at clip +0x24 through its slots 12, 14 and 16. It replaces the x, y and z floats of the vectors with the floats at +0x10, +0x1c and +0x28 where the flag bytes at +0x34 to +0x36, +0x38 to +0x3a and +0x3c to +0x3e are nonzero. When the scheduler test 0x00a1c050 is true it calls slot 18 of the target object with the three vectors and the scheduler origin. It then calls CharaActor setter 0x0065e660 with vector A and 0x0065e690 with vector B. Both receive the inverse of bit 0 of u8(D+0x37). Vector C reaches only the slot 18 call. Bytes +0x3b and +0x3f are not read.

Vector A is a position, vector B is a rotation in radians and vector C is a scale. The 33,078 install records hold A components between -2824.9 and 3563.5, B components within plus or minus pi and C components between 0.1 and 8.0. When CharaActor slot 154 returns 0, the setter 0x0065e660 stores the vector it receives at CharaActor +0x11f0. The roles of the slot 12, 14 and 16 vectors and of 0x0065e690 were not traced beyond the argument flow.

RaptureShowHideClip slot 1 at 0x0082de70 requires the actor record's slot 23 result to cast from IActor to RaptureActor and a nonnull pointer at RaptureActor +0x9c. It calls slot 2 of that pointer with the RaptureActor and the boolean u8(D+0x10) == 1. Slot 1 reads no record field beyond the actor ordinal and this byte. All 21,581 install records are 0x14 bytes and hold 0 or 1 at +0x10.

RaptureMotionClip slot 1 at 0x0082f120 ends the clip at once when s32(D+0x10) is negative. Otherwise it passes the index to slot 3 of the scheduler name object at +0x74, which fills a 16 byte name record. The table the clip builder reads at +0x0c of its owner is the table 0x00a27210 fills, because both use 8 byte entries with the string pointer at +0 and the entry is passed on as the class key. The owner object that holds the table was not traced. The role of the @CCPT entry byte +2, which equals 4 for LocalCameraClip in all 663 schedulers that list it, is UNKNOWN beyond this gate.
The object at RaptureActor +0x9c, whose slot 2 receives the ShowHideClip operand, was not identified. RaptureActor's constructor at 0x007ced70 does not store it.

The scheduler tick reads s16(D+8) through slot 22 as a filter against the object at scheduler +0x58, bit 2 of u8(D+0x0b) through slot 26 while scheduler +0xc8 is set, and bit 0 of u8(D+0x0b) through slot 25 for clips that already began. The callers of the accessors for u8(D+0x0a) and bit 1 of u8(D+0x0b) were not traced, and neither was the object behind slot 22. The fields of the classes listed in the manifest are only the ones read by slots 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8 named above. The Lay registry was not followed.

The scan reads 9,593 files below client/cut, finds 86,405 SEDB headers of which 689 fold to scb, and parses every scheduler. The 222,491 clip records use 102 classes. The twelve classes in this manifest are ranks 1 to 8 and 10 to 13 and hold 165,457 records. Rank 9 is BindActorClip. The full ranking is in cut-scheduler-clip-class-census.csv.

The invariants listed in the manifest hold for every record of their class: record sizes, flag bytes and enumerations, padding words, the ClipSyncClip and KillClip index ranges, the LocalCameraClip extension, the SetPosClip rotation range, the MotionClip scaled words, the PhysicsLookAtClip mode 1 angle range, the FacialPoseForSch name shape, the DepthOfFieldClip flag word and the @CCPT entry byte +2 of each class. The install section also pins the ShowHideClip operand, MotionClip speed and end order, PhysicsLookAtClip mode, ClipSyncClip count parity, NqMotionBlend switch, LipSync set, DepthOfField mode, Kill count and Mes route distributions, the SetPosClip position and scale ranges and the integer ranges of three word fields.

The Rapture group of 0x00635760 inserts RaptureMesClip (key 0x00fbc81c, factory 0x00638a60), RaptureNqMotionBlendOnOffClip (0x00fbcae0, 0x00639ab0), RaptureFacialLipSyncClip (0x00fbcf0c, 0x0063b1c0) and RaptureFacialPoseForSchClip (0x00fbcf68, 0x0063b370) through 0x0063f710. None of the four is preceded by a call to 0x0063f920 and none has a key in the base group. The base registrar 0x00a4c2a0 inserts DepthOfFieldClip (0x0109b580, 0x00a4ead0) and KillClip (0x0109b6d4, 0x00a4e210).

RaptureFacialLipSyncClip (key 0x00fbd3dc, site 0x0063715b) and KillClip (key 0x0109b6d4, site 0x00a4d08d) are inserted a second time with the same factory. Each second insert takes its registry operand from the result of a call to 0x00a65600 plus 8 immediately before it. The registry behind that call, and what reads it, were not walked.

RaptureNqMotionBlendOnOffClip slot 1 at 0x0081abc0 resolves the actor record, casts its slot 23 result from IActor to CharaActor and calls 0x0065d260 with the boolean u32(D+0x10) != 0 and u32(D+0x14). That method stores the value, or -1 when the boolean is false, at CharaActor +0x134c and passes it to 0x007ad020 with ECX at actor +0x4c0. 0x007ad020 converts two entry times from ticks to frames by multiplying by 30.0 and dividing by 300000.0 and compares the frame difference with the value. Slot 29 returns D+0x18, the record end.

The first word switches a blend on or off and the second is a length in motion frames. The install records hold 0 or 1 at +0x10 and a value of at most 500 at +0x14, with 15 in 10,335 of the 11,142 records. The role of the entry times inside 0x007ad020 was not traced.

RaptureFacialPoseForSchClip slot 1 at 0x00827140 casts the actor record to CharaActor and calls 0x0065e8d0 with the address D+0x10, s32(D+0x30) and s32(D+0x34). After the CharaActor slot 154 guard that method calls 0x007a6210 with ECX at actor +0x1bc and a fourth argument of -1. 0x007a6210 replaces a name that starts with off by cfxf_default, requires the bcm and btm lookups of 0x00662720 to succeed for any other name, copies at most 15 characters to +0x190, stores the low 16 bits of the first word with bit 16 set at +0x17c and stores the two numbers as floats at +0x174 and +0x178. Slot 29 returns D+0x38, the record end.

The 32 byte field is a facial pose resource name. All 9,081 install records hold a name that starts with cfxf_ and has at most 15 characters, followed by zero bytes. The meaning of the two trailing numbers was not traced beyond the stores.

RaptureFacialLipSyncClip slot 1 at 0x00826ab0 casts the actor record to CharaActor and calls 0x0065e980 with u32(D+0x10) and u32(D+0x14). After the CharaActor slot 154 guard that method calls 0x007a6fc0 with ECX at actor +0x35c. While the float at +0x1c of that component is positive, 0x007a6fc0 keeps only the first-word values 2 and 3, at +0x28 and +0x2c. Otherwise it stores both words, sets byte +0x30, picks the name at index (first == 1) + 2 * second of the table at 0x00fe7200 and resolves it through 0x00662720 with the bcm and btm tags into +0x10 and +0x14. Slot 29 returns D+0x18, the record end.

The table names are cfxl_lip_nor1, nor2, wis1, wis2, sho1 and sho2, so the second word selects a lip set and the first word a variant. The install records hold 0 to 7 in the first word, with 0 in 5,797 of the 7,441, and 0 to 2 in the second. The effect of the first-word values 4 to 7 was not traced.

RaptureMesClip slot 1 at 0x00813cf0 needs a target found through 0x00a20030 and 0x0060b360 and then reads the key entry byte +4. Value 2 copies u8(D+0x1c), u8(D+0x1d), u32(D+0x18) and u32(D+0x14). Value 3 does the same and then walks u32(D+0x20): bits 1 to 7 select entries of the object at scheduler +0xf0 through its slot 17 and bits 20 to 24 through its slot 29. Any other value returns after the base begin. A zero u8(D+0x1c) calls 0x00813f60, which posts message type 0xb of 0x14 bytes through 0x007ce7b0. A nonzero value calls 0x00813f10, which posts type 0xa of 0x1c bytes, and then calls slot 12 with 1 when u8(D+0x1d) is nonzero and 2 otherwise. Slot 3 at 0x00813bb0 calls 0x00a1c620 when the key entry byte is 2 or 3 and u8(D+0x1e) is nonzero. That function sets scheduler +0xc8 to 2 when it is 0. Slot 29 is the method shared with ShowHideClip and returns D+0x14, which is not the record end.

The receiver of the type 0xa and 0xb messages, the meaning of the words at +0x14 and +0x18, the entries selected by the +0x20 mask and the effect of scheduler +0xc8 beyond the tick test were not traced. All 6,301 install records have key entry byte 3, so the key 2 branch has no install data. The words at +0x10 and +0x1f are not read.

DepthOfFieldClip slot 1 at 0x00df0350 fetches the target object from the object at clip +0x24 and copies a 32 byte block from its slot 12. It moves bits 0, 1 and 4 to 10 of u32(D+0x14) into bits 0 to 8 of clip +0x38. With bit 1 set it passes u16(D+0x18) to scheduler lookup 0x00a20090 and builds a preset. With bit 1 clear each present bit replaces one of seven floats of the block with the floats at +0x18 to +0x30. Slot 1 ends by calling slot 13 of the target object with the clip and the block, whose first byte is bit 0 of clip +0x38. Slot 2 at 0x00df02e0 passes the elapsed ticks divided by the ticks per frame to 0x00df0120 when bits 0 and 1 are set. Slot 3 at 0x00df0050 sends the fetched block back with its first byte 0 when both bits are set. Slot 8 returns u32(D+0x10). Slot 29 returns D+0x34, which is 0x18 bytes past the end of a 0x1c byte record.

The seven floats are depth of field parameters and bit 1 selects a stored preset that is blended over the clip duration. The 5,780 parameter records have an end tick equal to the start tick. The 465 preset records are 0x1c bytes long and end after the start. The names rest on the class name and the argument flow.

KillClip slot 1 at 0x00dec7f0 reads the count n = s16(D+0x10) and, for each of n s16 indexes from D+0x14, calls the scheduler clip lookup 0x00a1ffb0. A clip that is found gets slot 18 called with 1, which sets its abort bit. A missing clip logs an error text with the index. Slot 29 returns D + ((2n + 0x19) & ~3), the rule of ClipSyncClip.
The class ends the clips it lists. The install records hold n from 0 to 19, and 229 records list an index of -1, which the lookup rejects. The 90 records with n = 0 list no clip.

The scheduler clock counts ticks. The constant 300000.0 at 0x00f67020 divided by a frame rate gives the ticks per frame, which the setter 0x00a20490 truncates into 0x012ed240, and 0x00a204b0 returns the inverse as a frame rate. The image value of 0x012ed240 is 10010, the truncation of 300000 / 29.97. The clock advance 0x00a204d0 adds the ticks per frame times the clock rate to the time at clock +8 once per frame step 0x00a1e540. It also consumes the pending delta at clock +0x10 once: the delta is added to the step, cleared, and a negative sum is clamped to 0 (setter and adder 0x00a203c0). 0x007ad020 converts ticks to motion frames at 30.0 per 300000.0. A tick is 1/300000 of a second and a frame is 300000 / f ticks for the frame rate f.

The float f passed to 0x00a20490 comes from slot 2 of the object returned by slot 4 of the object at [manager +0x74] + 4 in 0x00a025c0, and from the observer method 0x00a036e0. The concrete type and value were not traced, so the frame rate of a running client is UNKNOWN. The image value 10010 is the only static ticks per frame.

The start tick of a clip is slot 7, u32(D+4). The end tick is slot 8. The base slot 8 jumps through slot 7, so a class that does not override it has a duration of 0. MotionClip returns u32(D+0x18), DepthOfFieldClip u32(D+0x10) and LocalCameraClip u32(D+0x10) plus clip +0x110. Clip +0x110 starts at 0 and the LocalCameraClip update stores the change of scheduler origin word +0xa0 since the begin there only when bit 2 of u8(D+0x1a) is set behind the key entry gate. Slot 9 returns the elapsed ticks at clip +0x28.

0x00a1d330, called from 0x00a1e380 at 0x00a1e419, takes the scheduler time t as the clock time minus scheduler +0xa0 and +0x98. It walks the list at scheduler +0x30 from the cursor at scheduler +0x94 and stops at the first clip whose start tick is above t. A clip whose state is 0 or 4 begins when its start is not above t: slot 1 runs with a context that carries t - start, the base begin stores that overshoot as the elapsed ticks at clip +0x28, and the base update adds ticks per frame times the clock rate once per update. The tick updates each clip it began and the running pass 0x00a1e190 updates the clips in the list at scheduler +0x3c. Both end a clip by calling slot 3 and then slot 4 when the elapsed ticks are not below end - start, the state is 2 and the phase word is 0, or when the abort bit is set. The wrapper runs the running pass first, then the tick. The comparison of t with the start tick and the comparison of the elapsed ticks with end - start are signed 32 bit, so a clip whose end is below its start passes the end test on its first end check. Before the tick the wrapper tests scheduler slot 14 and bit 1 of the byte at scheduler +0x91 (0x00a1e3ab to 0x00a1e3f8): when slot 14 returns 1 and the bit is set, it clears the bit and adds one step, ticks per frame times the clock rate, to the 64 bit word at scheduler +0xa0, so t is held back one step. After the tick it walks the list at scheduler +0x3c (0x00a1e41e to 0x00a1e4bd) and, for each clip whose abort bit is set and whose slot 40 name is ActionClip, calls slot 3 and slot 4 and removes it from the list.

A begun clip with phase word 1 that is not ended is recorded through scheduler slot 15 (0x00a1d9b0) in the held list at scheduler +0x44, with head +0x48 and count +0x4c, and the tick adds t - start to scheduler origin word +0xa0 (0x00a1d8c5). While the held count is above 0 the wrapper 0x00a1e380 runs no tick and adds the step to +0xa0 instead (0x00a1e3a1 and 0x00a1e4d2), so the scheduler time does not advance. The running pass updates each held clip and ends it, with slot 3 and slot 4, when its state is 2 and its phase word is 0, without the duration test (0x00a1e2ac to 0x00a1e344). The phase word is clip +0x20, set by slot 12 and read by slot 13. ClipSyncClip, MotionClip and RaptureMesClip call slot 12.

The tick skips a clip when bit 1 of the byte at scheduler +0x90 is clear and slot 30 returns true (0x00a1d44f to 0x00a1d464). Slot 30 is 0x00b73290, which loads 1 and returns, in the primary vtable of all twelve documented classes (vtable +0x78). A documented clip therefore begins only while bit 1 of scheduler +0x90 is set.

The code that sets bit 1 of the byte at scheduler +0x90 and the code that sets bit 1 of the byte at scheduler +0x91 are UNKNOWN, as is the code that returns a RaptureMesClip phase word from 1 to 0 or sets its abort bit. A phase 1 RaptureMesClip holds the scheduler time under the documented rules until one of them runs.

The list builder 0x00a28210 appends, for each clip record of a block, the entry at index s16(D+0x0c) of the list of all clips of the scheduler to the list at scheduler +0x30. 0x00a28510 builds the list of all clips block by block in record order, and slot 20 returns the index word. The clip lookup used by ClipSyncClip and KillClip indexes the same list.

Which block the scheduler plays and how it is chosen, the callers of 0x00a1ba90, the block header fields, the use of scheduler +0x1cc, how often 0x00a1e540 repeats the wrapper in one frame step, the seek branches of the tick and the frame rate source were not traced.

Every one of the 222,491 clip records has a start tick that is a multiple of 10000 and an s16(D+0x0c) equal to its index in the scheduler clip list. Within a block the start ticks do not decrease, over 213,369 pairs. The MotionClip end tick is above the start in 21,988 records, equal in 38 and below in 59, so a negative duration occurs, and 19,529 end ticks are multiples of 10000. The LocalCameraClip end is never below the start and 11 records set bit 2 of u8(D+0x1a). The DepthOfFieldClip end equals the start in all 5,780 parameter records and is above it in all 465 preset records.

Manager slot 3 at 0x00635760 inserts RaptureNqIdleSetClip (factory 0x00639a20), RaptureAutoMoveClip (0x00638790), RaptureBlackFadeClip (0x006395a0), RaptureSoundClip (0x00639b40), RaptureScaleClip (0x0063ac20), RaptureTurnClip (0x00638670) and RaptureBgmClip (0x00639d80) through 0x0063f710 with no erase call and no base group key. It inserts ActionClip (0x0063c210) after an erase call 0x0063f920 with a second copy of the key literal. The base registrar 0x00a4c2a0 inserts ActionClip with the factory 0x00a4dd40 at 0x00a4c4c9 and again at 0x00a4cf7c. RaptureSoundClip is inserted a second time at 0x006372e1 with the same factory through the registry of 0x00a65600.

The factories store the object sizes 0x38 for RaptureNqIdleSetClip, RaptureScaleClip and RaptureBgmClip, 0x40 for RaptureAutoMoveClip and RaptureBlackFadeClip, 0x54 for RaptureSoundClip, 0x68 for ActionClip and 0x3c for RaptureTurnClip. Each constructor chain ends in 0x00a21260 and installs the primary vtable at +0 and a secondary table at +8. The RTTI name of ActionClip is RaptureActionClip.

RaptureNqIdleSetClip slot 1 passes the address D+0x10 to CharaActor method 0x0065e3e0, which copies the string into a 16 byte buffer and passes it to 0x0065c4c0. The record is 0x30 bytes and slot 29 returns D+0x30.
The string names the idle motion set. The name 0x0065c4c0 binds to the keys cbnm_id0 and cbbm_id0 follows from the call arguments. The effect of the state object after the rebind was not traced.

RaptureAutoMoveClip slot 1 reads the fields at D+0x10 to D+0x26, builds a position list from the curves tx, ty and tz of the track record named by u16(D+0x26) and hands a parameter block to CharaActor method 0x0065eaf0. Slot 2 follows the move through 0x0065eb60 and its seek branch sets the position through 0x0065e660.
The track record holds a movement path and f32(D+0x20) is its speed. The names rest on the argument flow into the path builder 0x007ae8b0 and the strings tx, ty and tz.

The meaning of the words at D+0x14, D+0x16, D+0x18 and D+0x1c after the handoff, the scheduler chunk behind the table of 0x00a20090 and the effect of CharaActor method 0x0065eaf0 on the actor were not traced.

RaptureBlackFadeClip slot 1 selects a float4 from a two entry pointer table with u32(D+0x14), converts s32(D+0x18) frames to ticks at 30 frames per second and passes both to 0x00612400 with the object at +0x6c of the owner result. Slot 2 ends the clip when the scheduler frame number reaches the begin frame plus the frames.
Entry 0 of the table is opaque black and entry 1 is clear black, so the clip fades the screen toward one of them. Which direction each selector gives was not traced.

RaptureSoundClip reads the key entry byte +4 and takes the resource id from D+0x14 for 0, from D+0x18 for 1 and from the array at D+0x28 for 2 and 3. The array length is u32(D+0x24) in bytes. The play entry 0x007cf100 receives the slot number, the resource id, the volume and two more words. The start helper returns true only for a nonzero slot on the array path, so a slot 0 clip ends with phase 0 after its start.
The array entries are sound resource ids and the clip plays one of them. The meaning of the flag word bits and of the selector 0x006b6cd0 is inferred from their use as index sources.

The sound objects behind the slot number, the global counters 0x0134e2a8 and 0x0134e2ac that bit 3 of the flag word feeds, the receiver of u32(D+0x20) and the key 0 and 1 branches are not in the install and were not traced beyond the call arguments. What ends a clip of nonzero slot is also not known.

ActionClip slot 1 and the shared begin 0x00a18170 read the action id at D+0x10, bits 3 and 7 of u8(D+0x14) and the words at D+0x1c and D+0x20. Slot 8 returns D+0x18 as the end tick and slot 30 returns false.
The clip starts an actor action by id and the looping branch repeats it. The names rest on the lookup call shape and the error texts.

The object returned by 0x00a20040, the action tables behind the lookup methods, the two start methods chosen by bit 3, the writers of clip +0x44 and the bytes D+0x15 and D+0x24 to D+0x27 are not decoded.

RaptureScaleClip slot 1 requires a CharaActor, switches on the key entry byte +4 with the values 0 and 1 and the mode word at D+0x14, and calls 0x00662b20, 0x0065e390 or 0x0065e320 with the words of the selected layout.
Mode 0 selects a size preset by index and mode 1 sets a uniform scale factor. The unit of the length word was not traced.

RaptureTurnClip slot 1 passes f32(D+0x10) to CharaActor method 0x0065e4a0 and slot 2 waits on the predicate 0x007a4cc0 for up to 90 updates. Slot 2 begins with the base begin 0x00a20f30 instead of the base update.
The float is a target direction in radians. The scaling by 16777216 over the float 2 pi into a 24 bit direction is read from 0x007b0530.
RaptureBgmClip slot 1 forwards u32(D+0x20), s32(D+0x14), s32(D+0x18) and a flag that is true when the actor record class is ProxyActor to 0x00611900 and so to 0x0060f630.
The values are a music resource id in the 0x07fe0000 range and a fade time. The meaning of the flag beyond its use in 0x0060f630 was not traced.

The eight classes read the start tick u32(D+4) and all but ActionClip use the base end tick method 0x00a21080. ActionClip slot 8 returns u32(D+0x18). RaptureBlackFadeClip converts the scheduler clock to a frame number with 0x00a203e0.
Slot 30 of ActionClip is 0x005c5c80, which returns false, so the begin test of the scheduler tick never skips an ActionClip for a clear bit 1 of S+0x90.

classes.name: MotionClip
classes.control: Slot 1 and slot 2 call slot 18 with 1 and slot 12 with 0 or 2.

classes.name: ClipSyncClip
classes.control: Slot 1 calls slot 12 with 1. Slot 2 calls slot 12 with 0 once the listed clips are done.

classes.name: RaptureMesClip
classes.control: Slot 1 calls slot 12 with 1 or 2 after the type 0xa post.

classes.name: KillClip
classes.control: Slot 1 calls slot 18 with 1 on the listed clips, not on itself.

classes.name: RaptureAutoMoveClip
classes.control: Slot 1 calls slot 12 with 2 after the handoff. Slot 2 calls slot 12 with 2 while 0x0065eb60 reports a move in progress and with 0 when it does not or when the clip is aborted.

classes.name: RaptureBlackFadeClip
classes.control: Slot 1 calls slot 12 with 2 and records the begin frame. Slot 2 calls slot 12 with 0 once the scheduler frame number reaches the begin frame plus the fade frames.

classes.name: RaptureSoundClip
classes.control: Slot 2 starts the sound once. It calls slot 12 with 0 when the start helper returns false, which holds for every slot 0 clip, and with 2, or 1 for a preload clip, when it returns true for a nonzero slot, and with 0 after an abort. Slot 1 calls slot 12 with 2 when bit 2 of S+0x91 is set.

classes.name: ActionClip
classes.control: Slot 1 ends at u32(D+0x18). Slot 2 calls slot 12 with 0 when clip +0x44 is not -1 and equals the pass counter at clip +0x58. Slot 30 returns false so the begin does not wait for S+0x90 bit 1.

classes.name: RaptureTurnClip
classes.control: Slot 1 calls slot 12 with 2. Slot 2 starts with the base begin 0x00a20f30, then calls slot 12 with 2 while the turn predicate holds within 90 updates and calls slot 18 with 1 and slot 12 with 0 otherwise.
